title: Mirror calmly when someone is angry
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What does your face do when you are corrected?
I said that the chapter talks about mirroring: when someone is angry, what should your demeanor be? Mirroring means matching gestures, tone and pace.
A student said that when a colleague corrected him sharply, he listened with wide eyes, used his hands, said you are right, I am sorry, and let the colleague finish, like a teapot letting off steam.
Another said that she had made a similar mistake with a recipe she was given, which caused an argument with the others.
I said: even if I am getting fired, I know why, and the person did not make me feel bad about it. Do you not want to have control of that?
I said that in that interaction you are aligning their potential with their discipline, and their perception with their actions.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the last time you were corrected.
Write what your face and hands did.
Write what you would do to stay calm.
Write what you would say after they finish.
Write what you learned from the correction.

check.q: What did I say mirroring is?
What did the student do when corrected?
choices: Listened and let the colleague finish

check.q: What did I say you align?

recap: Mirror, let them finish, stay in control.
